messages:
eli: CI started failing on Windows embeddable Python 3.8 when tests import AsyncClient. Linux passes. Stack trace below — looks like certifi is referenced but not installed in the minimal embeddable image. Anyone else hit packaging gaps like this?

eli: ```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/test_connect.py", line 8, in test_connect
    client = AsyncClient(api_key="x")
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 34, in __init__
    self._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(ssl=self._build_ssl_context())
  File "/opt/venv/lib/python3.8/site-packages/redwood/async_client.py", line 78, in _build_ssl_context
    ctx.load_verify_locations(cafile=certifi.where())
NameError: name 'certifi' is not defined
```

rachael: That NameError means certifi isn't imported or available. Embeddable builds often have a minimal set of packages so transitive deps don't always exist.

tim: Looked at setup.cfg/wheel metadata: certifi is only in extras_require["ssl"]. That's the culprit 50d. Most dev envs get it transitively from requests but embeddable CI doesn't.

eli: Short-term hack: add a guarded import and fallback to ssl.create_default_context() so we don't crash at import time. But we should still prefer certifi when available.

tim: Proposed patch: in redwood/async_client.py, try `import certifi` except: set certifi=None, then in _build_ssl_context load certifi.where() if present and log which bundle we used. Add identical behavior to sync client.

sam: Agreed. Also our type stubs are missing AsyncClient in top-level exports and lack __aenter__/__aexit__ signatures which makes IDEs unhappy. Let's update py.typed / __all__ and add those method signatures to stubs.

rachael: I'll create a canonical issue listing: 1) move certifi to install_requires 2) defensive import + fallback 3) add unit test that uninstalls certifi and asserts no NameError 4) update typing exports and async context manager signatures 5) add GH Actions matrix job for windows-embeddable-3.8.

devx-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/issues/1302 (certifi packaging + async NameError + typing exports). Docs todo added: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/python#windows-embeddable (note about certs).

eli: Tests I ran locally: after adding guarded import, the client now raises an SSL error (expected) instead of NameError when certifi isn't installed. Good.

tim: I'll open PR to move certifi to install_requires and add the defensive import snippet. Also adding a small debug log: `logger.debug('Using cert bundle: %s', certifi.where())` when certifi loaded.

rachael: For the CI job, we should explicitly install the embeddable python build and create a venv without certifi to reproduce. Might be flaky but helpful to catch regressions.

sam: One more DX note: update quickstart to recommend `python -m pip install certifi` on Windows embeddable or use SDK v0.13+ which will handle certs gracefully. That will reduce onboarding friction.

eli: Thanks all 44d. This saved our Windows CI.

devx-bot: Linked PR template checklist: add tests + update stubs + docs blurb.
